title: Ensembler: Protect Collaborative Inference Privacy from Model Inversion Attack via Selective Ensemble
problem: Collaborative inference allows cloud providers to reconstruct sensitive client inputs via model inversion attacks; existing defenses either sacrifice privacy or add prohibitive overhead.
motivation: Privacy in collaborative DNN inference is essential for healthcare, finance; current split-learning exposes gradient information enabling inversion.
method: Uses selective ensemble on server-side: multiple model branches ensemble predictions to obfuscate gradient signals, making input reconstruction harder while maintaining inference accuracy with <5% overhead.
key_novelty: Selective ensemble-based privacy defense that exploits model diversity to hide input signatures in collaborative inference.
contributions: Ensembler framework for privacy-preserving collaborative inference
Selective model ensemble to obfuscate input reconstruction
4.8% inference time overhead for privacy guarantee
limitations: Not discussed; evaluation limited to image classification, generalization to other modalities unclear.
